source_name: ČNB – supervisory opinions on payment regulation (stanoviska)
why_relevant: ČNB opinions interpret when an e-money institution needs authorisation for card-acquiring-type services (e.g. RS2023-07). These define the regulatory perimeter that shapes which PSPs can offer acquiring in CZ — an early indicator of market-structure change.

source_name: SumUp Česko (cs-cz product pages)
why_relevant: Leading mPOS/softPOS challenger to bank terminal estates in CZ, with retail distribution (DATART) — i.e. terminals sold off the shelf, bypassing bank sales channels. Key competitor signal for anyone tracking the CZ terminal estate.

source_name: Dotypay / Dotykačka – integrated POS + payment terminal
why_relevant: Czech POS-plus-payments player bundling terminals with cash-register software (STPAY app). Represents the 'POS vendor as payments distributor' channel that competes with bank acquiring for SME merchants.

source_name: Payten / Sonet (paytenpos.cz) – POS specifications
why_relevant: Sonet, member of the Payten (Asseco) group, is a long-standing Czech POS/terminal software and integration house. Its POS specification pages document which terminal hardware and acquirer protocols are supported — a technical map of the CZ terminal estate and a direct competitor set for terminal vendors.

source_name: ERP/ECR vendor terminal-integration help pages (Stormware Pohoda, ABRA Flexi, KASAmax)
why_relevant: Accounting/cash-register vendors document exactly which acquirers and terminal models they certify against (Global Payments/ČS, KB SmartPay, ČSOB, UniCredit, Comgate Nexgo, SumUp; Ingenico iCT220/Desk3200/Move2500, Verifone VX520/VX675). They also expose acquirer-specific behavioural rules (e.g. KB and ČSOB blocking manual entry in CASHREGISTER mode). This is a REVEALS-INDIRECTLY layer that enumerates the estate without any acquirer publishing it.

source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci + data.apek.cz
why_relevant: CZ e-commerce association (founded 1998) with a member directory and a data portal covering online payments, e-shop counts and market share. Membership list is a POINTER to gateways/PSPs active in CZ e-commerce; the data portal gives market context for payment-method mix.

source_name: Lupa.cz – payments/e-commerce tag pages
why_relevant: Czech internet-industry trade press with persistent topic tags for payment systems and APEK. Reliable running commentary on gateway launches, PSD2/SCA rollouts and CZ fintech entries, often naming deals that never get a press release.

source_name: ČTK Protext / ČeskéNoviny.cz – paid press-release wire
why_relevant: Czech news agency wire where payments actors (SBK, banks, PSPs) place full-text press releases that are otherwise scattered or absent from corporate sites. Acts as a single aggregation point and archive for CZ payments announcements.

source_name: Pays.cz – small Czech gateway, Shoptet add-on and pricing transparency
why_relevant: Long-tail domestic gateway that competes on 'no monthly fee' positioning and publishes comparative blog content on terminal brands. Useful for mapping the second tier of CZ gateways below Comgate/GoPay/ThePay and for pricing benchmarks.

source_name: Shopify App Store – Czech payment gateway apps (cs locale)
why_relevant: International platform marketplace that lists CZ-specific gateway apps (GoPay, Comgate). Cross-checks the Shoptet directory and shows which Czech PSPs invest in reaching merchants on global platforms — a partnership-strategy signal.

source_name: ČNB – CERTIS (systém mezibankovního platebního styku) hub
source_subtype: central bank / payment system operator portal
why_relevant: Root node of the Czech national clearing infrastructure. Links out to scheme rules, participant lists, instant-payment description, technical annexes and bank codes — the single best entry point for enumerating every institution technically connected to CZK rails, and for spotting scheme changes that force bank-side IT projects (a demand signal for vendors).

source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků okamžitých plateb (PDF, versioned)
why_relevant: Authoritative, version-numbered roster of banks that have joined the CZK instant-payment scheme (search result indicated Version 20, effective 23 Mar 2026). Version-over-version diffs reveal exactly which institution went live when — a precise, dateable proxy for completed instant-payment implementation projects and therefore for vendor wins.

source_name: ČNB – Pravidla platebního systému CERTIS (scheme rulebook + annexes)
why_relevant: The binding technical/operational rulebook (search results showed Version 14, effective 19 May 2025) plus numbered annexes including testing procedures. Rule changes and new annexes are the upstream trigger for bank IT change programmes; the testing annex reveals certification obligations that third-party suppliers must satisfy.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – Český standard pro Open banking (COBS)
why_relevant: COBS is the uniquely Czech API standard that essentially all CZ banks implement; it is the specification any integration vendor must build against. Rulebook versions (a v0.4.1 rulebook PDF and later versions are referenced by implementers) mark the technical goalposts that drive bank API projects.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace – ČBA Online (association hub, news & expert commissions)
why_relevant: The standards body itself: member list, expert commissions (payments, digitalisation, security), position papers and press releases. Association outputs pre-announce standard changes months before banks tender for them, and speaker lists at ČBA events expose which vendors are inside the tent.

source_name: Bank iD (Bankovní identita, a.s.) – official site, incl. company/implementation section
why_relevant: Operator of the uniquely Czech bank-identity scheme. Bank members named in sources: Česká spořitelna, Komerční banka, ČSOB, Air Bank, MONETA Money Bank, mBank, Raiffeisenbank, Fio banka. The 'pro firmy / implementace' section describes onboarding and points to implementation partners — the closest thing to a relying-party and integrator directory in the Czech market. Usage scale reported at ~5m users (Aug 2025) rising to ~5.3m by H1 2026.

source_name: Bank member banks' press-release rooms as BankID/instant-payment announcement channel
why_relevant: Banks announce infrastructure milestones and named relying parties in their own press rooms — e.g. KB's release on opening Bank ID to commercial entities with ČEZ as the first, and Česká spořitelna's release on being the first bank to offer digital signing for companies via bank identity. These releases date partnerships precisely and often name the technology supplier.

source_name: Komerční banka – KB API / PSD2 developer portal (bank-level API spec)
why_relevant: Representative example of a bank's own API documentation and sandbox guides (e.g. a PISP 1SCA sandbox manual PDF). Bank developer portals expose API versioning, conformance to COBS, and sometimes the platform branding — a direct technical read on each bank's stack.

source_name: Portál Identity občana / info.identita.gov.cz – NIA qualified provider & service-provider registry
why_relevant: The state eID hub (run by DIA) publishes the list of qualified identity providers and qualified service providers connected to the national node — the register in which Bank iD and mojeID sit alongside every relying party in the public sector. Enumerates the demand side of Czech digital identity, invisible in vendor marketing.

source_name: mojeID (Sdružení CZ.NIC) – identity provider site and public-administration integration pages
why_relevant: mojeID is the non-bank qualified eID competing with Bank iD; CZ.NIC obtained Ministry of Interior accreditation and connected to NIA at the 'substantial' assurance level. Its support/integration pages and CZ.NIC conference decks document the certification path and the relying parties adopting it.

source_name: Architektura eGovernmentu ČR (archi.gov.cz) – NAP architecture pages incl. NIA
why_relevant: The national enterprise-architecture wiki documents how eID, the national node and connected registries are supposed to fit together, including planned components. It reveals state-side architectural direction (and therefore future procurement) ahead of any tender notice.

source_name: European Payments Council – Register of Participants (SCT Inst / SCT / SDD)
why_relevant: Pan-European adherence register listing every PSP that has joined each SEPA scheme, downloadable and filterable by country. For CZ it shows which Czech PSPs are already SEPA-instant capable ahead of the euro instant-payments obligations, i.e. who has already completed (or must still run) a SEPA Inst project.

source_name: EBA CLEARING – RT1 and STEP2 participant lists
why_relevant: Names the PSPs settling euro instant payments via RT1 (search result noted UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia among RT1 participants/addressable PSPs). Together with the STEP2 list and the admission page, it shows which Czech-market banks reach euro rails directly versus via a sponsor — a direct read on cross-border payment capability gaps.

source_name: ECB – digital euro project pages, Rulebook Development Group progress reports
why_relevant: Publishes the draft scheme rulebook (v0.91 published 2 July 2026 per the RDG progress report; sections 8, 9 and annex F1 still placeholders to be developed in H2 2026) and reports on component-provider and service-supplier selection from the preparation phase. Even for a non-euro CZ, this sets the technical template Czech banks and vendors will have to meet, and the supplier shortlists name the competitive field.

source_name: ČNB – Instant payments (EN) / euro instant payments obligation pages
why_relevant: English-language ČNB explanation of the CZK instant scheme and of the euro instant-payment obligations — search results indicate domestic banks must offer euro instant payments from July 2027 (euro payments from CZK accounts from June 2028), explicitly outside CERTIS. That deadline is the single clearest forward-looking demand driver in the CZ payments infrastructure market.

source_name: Měšec.cz – okamžité platby: bank-by-bank coverage and limits
why_relevant: Consumer-finance portal maintaining a comparative table of which Czech banks offer instant payments and at what limits, plus news items dating each rollout (e.g. instant payments to ČNB accounts). Useful as a fast, human-readable cross-check on the official ČNB participant list and as a timeline of go-lives.

source_name: Lupa.cz – Bankovní identita topic hub (critical tech journalism)
why_relevant: Sustained, technically literate coverage of Bank iD adoption, including critical analysis of which commercial providers actually support login versus only one-off identity verification. Fills the gap where the scheme operator's own marketing does not distinguish depth of integration.

source_name: eGovernment conference proceedings (egovernment.cz) – ČBA payments presentations
why_relevant: Publishes downloadable slide decks from Czech public-sector/banking events, including a ČBA presentation on PSD2 outcomes by Tomáš Hladek. Conference decks by association and central-bank staff routinely contain roadmap detail and architecture diagrams absent from official web pages.
